mechanism: Both names are DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS rows (src/config-options.lisp:438), so neither reaches START-NODE and neither has a reader. The startup sequence in START-NODE runs %INIT-LOAD-CHAIN, %INIT-RECOVER-CHAIN, %INIT-SERVICES, %FINISH-INIT-AND-START-SYNC, %START-NETWORK-SERVICES and %IMPORT-EXTERNAL-BLOCK-FILES (src/node/init.lisp:1492-1502) and calls nothing that re-reads and re-checks stored blocks; %INIT-RECOVER-CHAIN (:695-725) resolves a torn flush and the assumeutxo snapshot chainstate, which is crash recovery, not verification. The only verification mechanism in the tree is the verifychain RPC (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:775-806), it has no startup caller (grep for verify-chain/verifychain/verify-db across src/ returns only that definition and the two RPC tables at src/rpc/core-tables.lisp:115, :354), and it implements level 0/1 only -- re-read the block, recompute the merkle root, re-check PoW -- with no undo-data check, no disconnect and no reconnect against the UTXO set. Core at d3056bc reads both with GetIntArg into ChainstateLoadOptions (init.cpp:1388-1389), sets options.require_full_verification = IsArgSet("-checkblocks") || IsArgSet("-checklevel") (:1390), and VerifyLoadedChainstate runs CVerifyDB::VerifyDB before the node is up, turning VerifyDBResult::SKIPPED_L3_CHECKS into ChainstateLoadStatus::FAILURE_INSUFFICIENT_DBCACHE precisely when the operator asked (node/chainstate.cpp:257-274).
consequence: Judged on the OPTION contract only, as scoped: an operator who sets -checkblocks/-checklevel after an unclean shutdown asks for a proof the chainstate is sound and gets no verification -- but is told so. The startup WARN names both options by name, is the first line of debug.log and also reaches the console, so the belief the operator would otherwise hold is corrected before the node finishes coming up. Core additionally treats these as DEBUG_ONLY arguments (init.cpp:640-641), hidden from -help without -help-debug, so the audience is narrower than an ordinary operator option. That makes this dimension's half an observability gap, S3: the option is accepted and announced-as-ignored rather than silently doing something else, and there is no durability or disk-space consequence that follows from SETTING the option as opposed to from the default. The durable consequence -- that no VerifyDB runs AT ALL, which in Core happens by default at -checkblocks=6 -checklevel=3 with no option set, so the exposure exists on every start of every node and is not created by this option -- belongs to the validation-storage verifier's finding 4452772a and is deliberately not scored here. Nothing in this verdict should be read as reducing that one; if 4452772a lands, the correct fix closes both and the option rows come back with it.

fix_shape: The option contract cannot be honoured before the mechanism exists, so this is the second half of 4452772a and should be fixed with it, not before it. Once a CVerifyDB equivalent exists (levels 1-4: re-read and CheckBlock each block, read and check its undo data, disconnect it and reconnect it against the coins view, bounded by the coins cache the way Core bounds it), wire it into %INIT-LOAD-CHAIN before the node is declared up and before %INIT-SERVICES opens the RPC, driven by two real DEFINE-OPTION rows -- checkblocks defaulting to 6 and checklevel to 3, Core's DEFAULT_CHECKBLOCKS/DEFAULT_CHECKLEVEL -- with 0 meaning "all blocks" as Core's help text says. Carry Core's require_full_verification: record whether either option was EXPLICITLY supplied (which needs a supplied-p distinct from the default, since the values themselves cannot express it) and, when it was, turn a level-3 downgrade into a fatal INIT-ERROR rather than a log line, mirroring FAILURE_INSUFFICIENT_DBCACHE. Reuse the verifychain RPC's body as the level-0/1 core so the two paths cannot diverge, and remove both names from DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS in the same commit so the startup WARN stops naming them. Until that lands, the honest interim is to leave the WARN exactly as it is -- it is what makes this S3 rather than S2.
